content:
The image shows seedling-stage soybean plants pulled from soil. Key observations:

- Soil is wet/muddy — high moisture conditions
- One seedling on the left appears mostly green/healthy still
- The center seedling shows a cross-section of the hypocotyl: the outer tissue is brown/necrotic while inner tissue is still green — this is a browning/rotting of the outer stem tissue
- The rightmost piece shows a completely brown, decomposed stem/root cross-section
- Tissue appears soft and rotted, not dry or firm
- Soil is clinging to the roots
- No firm, dry cankers (rules out Rhizoctonia)
- No reddish-brown sunken lesions at soil line

The pattern here is seedling damping-off with water-soaked, soft brown rot of the hypocotyl/root tissue in wet, muddy conditions. The soft rot with water-soaked appearance, combined with the very wet soil conditions, points strongly to Pythium damping-off rather than Rhizoctonia (which causes firm, dry, reddish-brown cankers) or Phytophthora (which tends to show chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward in older plants).
